title: Universal filtration truncations and their distinguished triangles
statement:
Let $\mathcal C$ be an abelian category [def-sp-abelian], with localizations taken in a common larger universe. Let $DF^+(\mathcal C)$ be the localization of bounded-below cochain complexes [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] with a finite decreasing filtration by subcomplexes [def-sp-filtration, def-sp-filtered-complex-subquotients] at maps that are quasi-isomorphisms on every graded complex. Finite means that $F^aM=M$ and $F^{b+1}M=0$ for some integers $a\le b$, independently of cochain degree. This localization has the triangulated structure [def-weil-triangulated-category] induced by filtered mapping cones. Forgetting the filtration $\omega:DF^+(\mathcal C)\to D^+(\mathcal C)$ and each graded-piece functor $\operatorname{gr}^p:DF^+(\mathcal C)\to D^+(\mathcal C)$ are exact.

For every integer $r$, the subcomplex truncation $t_{\ge r}M=F^rM$ and quotient truncation $t_{<r}M=M/F^rM$, with induced and quotient filtrations, descend to exact functors. They have graded pieces respectively $\operatorname{gr}^pM$ for $p\ge r$ and $p<r$, and zero otherwise. Write $DF^{+,\ge r}$ and $DF^{+,<r}$ for the full subcategories whose graded pieces vanish for $p<r$ and $p\ge r$, respectively. There is a natural distinguished triangle $t_{\ge r}M\xrightarrow{\iota_{r,M}}M\xrightarrow{q_{r,M}}t_{<r}M\to(t_{\ge r}M)[1]$, induced by the subcomplex inclusion and quotient. It is uniquely determined, up to unique isomorphism inducing the identity on $M$, among distinguished triangles $L\to M\to R\to L[1]$ with $L\in DF^{+,\ge r}$ and $R\in DF^{+,<r}$.

For $L\in DF^{+,\ge r}$ and $R\in DF^{+,<r}$, the canonical maps $\operatorname{Hom}(L,t_{\ge r}M)\xrightarrow{\iota_{r,M}\circ -}\operatorname{Hom}(L,M)$ and $\operatorname{Hom}(t_{<r}M,R)\xrightarrow{-\circ q_{r,M}}\operatorname{Hom}(M,R)$ are bijective, naturally in their arguments. Thus $t_{\ge r}$ is right adjoint to the inclusion of $DF^{+,\ge r}$, and $t_{<r}$ is left adjoint to the inclusion of $DF^{+,<r}$.

Put $T_p=t_{\ge p}t_{<p+1}$. This functor has only the graded piece $\operatorname{gr}^pM$, and $\omega T_p=\operatorname{gr}^p$ canonically and naturally. On the full subcategory with all other graded pieces zero, the truncation maps identify $T_p$ with the identity, and forgetting filtration is an equivalence to $D^+(\mathcal C)$, inverse to placing a complex in filtration degree $p$. All assertions use vanishing in the derived category, so apply even when the other graded complexes are acyclic rather than literally zero.

proof.text: Take the normalized construction of high, low, omega, and gr, their actual representative comparisons, canonical graded projection, and distinguished triangle. All these fields are retained unchanged in the completed package.

Identify the source category of uniformly finite bounded-below filtered complexes with UniformFilteredComplexes A none (CochainComplex.plus A): strict lower bounds in DegreeBound and IsStrictlyGE are equivalent. The two inverse functors induce an equivalence of their localizations by Mathlib Localization.uniq. Compose with the bounded-below to unbounded comparison, which is fully faithful. Localization uniqueness and the representative gr and omega comparisons give natural isomorphisms intoUnbounded ⋙ gr_U^a ≅ gr_D^a ⋙ Plus.ι and intoUnbounded ⋙ omega_U ≅ omega_D ⋙ Plus.ι.

In the unbounded model, an object with all grades zero is zero: regard it as pure in grade zero; pureComparison shows its underlying object is zero and the fully faithful pure-grade equivalence reflects zero. If R is low-supported at p, high_p R has every grade zero, using high_support below p and high_grade plus the support of R at or above p. Therefore high_p R is zero. The unbounded high_hom_bijective implies that Hom(L,R) is a singleton for high-supported L. Pull this assertion back along the fully faithful comparison. Because gr_D commutes with cochain shifts, L[1] has the same support, proving also that Hom(L[1],R) is a singleton.

Apply triangle_morphism_extension to the canonical distinguished triangle and the contractible triangles L→L→0 and 0→R→R. The two singleton Hom assertions make the relevant composite zero and give uniqueness of the first or third component. These are precisely the two desired Hom bijections. Their naturality is associativity together with naturality of inclusion and quotient. Compare two supported distinguished triangles by extending the identity middle map in both directions. Singleton shifted cross-Homs give equality of all triangle morphisms with that middle component. Their composites are identities, giving the unique isomorphism of triangles with middle component the identity.

Restrict the fully faithful comparison to the full pure-grade subcategories. The natural omega comparison and full faithfulness of the unbounded pure-grade equivalence and of Plus.ι imply that omega_D on pure objects is fully faithful. Given K in D⁺(A), choose a pure unbounded object M with omega_U M≅K. Its only surviving grade is p and is isomorphic to K by pureComparison; all its graded homologies therefore vanish below one common bound. Using a complex representative and grComparison transports this to uniformLocalizedSupport. The essential-image clause of the bounded localization comparison supplies a bounded-below filtered preimage. Graded comparisons and reflection of zero by Plus.ι make this preimage pure. Full faithfulness of Plus.ι pulls the underlying isomorphism back to D⁺(A). Thus omega_D is essentially surjective as well. Take the inverse of this equivalence for place; its counit gives place_forget and its codomain subtype gives place_grade. Assemble all fields of FilteredTruncationData.

from.place: Step 3, paragraph 'More precisely, they form an endomorphism of this triangle of filtered origin': the exact compact-support filtered functors must recover the ordinary functors on each graded piece; universal filtration truncations supply that comparison.

split_report.summary: Split the generic finite-filtered bounded-below localization into six proof steps: the triangulated localization of uniformly filtered complexes, descent and exactness of truncations/forgetful and graded functors, the cone realization of the truncation triangle, roof-level semiorthogonality and the two universal Hom bijections by triangle-morphism extension, uniqueness by triangle comparison, and the pure-grade equivalence. No new child nodes or Mathlib leaves were needed. The adjoint labels in Varshavsky §5.1.1(c) are reversed; the item statement and proof use the corrected universal maps.
